gpt.text:
Run the three commands in the order shown; they’re already a sensible “advance the state” sequence:

1) **Pick and run the best module candidate (AUB autopilot)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
- Uses `module_registry.yaml` to enumerate module-level candidates.
- `--run` executes evaluations.
- `--select-best` promotes the best-performing candidate (i.e., tries to create a new PASS candidate / update whatever your pipeline uses as “current best”).

2) **Run system-level candidates (end-to-end)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
- Evaluates full system configurations defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.
- Useful even if module-level didn’t produce a PASS—this explores system combos directly.

3) **Generate the “next fix” plan/report**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
- Produces a markdown report with recommended next interventions, based on what’s in the registry and recent results.

### Practical notes / quick checks
- Make sure you’re at repo root and your environment is active (venv/conda), then consider:
  - Confirm Python version expected by the project.
  - Ensure any required API keys / dataset paths are set (often via `.env` or exported vars).
- If you want a single copy/paste block:
```bash
set -e
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

If you paste the stdout/stderr from any step that fails (or the directory where results get written), I can help diagnose and interpret what got selected and whether it improved over the current champion’s tuning/lockbox means.
